notes.title: Demo Updates and Fixes
notes.notes:
As players try out the demo I've received some feedback about various things. Stuff ranging from bugs to adjustments they would like to maybe see. I don't want to wait for the full release to make some of those adjustments so I will periodically push updates to the demo in an effort to create the best experience for the demo as possible. To reiterate my earlier news post, the demo is a vertical slice of what I would like for the full game to be and it's in the spirit of that effort that I'd like to take feedback and make adjustments where I can. For anyone experiencing issues I do apologize and know that I will do my best to correct where I can.

My most recent update includes some of the below changes.
[list]
[*] Enemy AI fix for animations causing character to behave in unexpected ways
[*] Mouse and Keyboard support for one of the interaction objects found in the game
[*] Various UI improvements: There have been some issues with focus between controller and Mouse that created all kinds of issues related to UI stuff
[*] Linux Support: The game is supported on Linux although the store may not reflect that info right now. The Linux support is new
[*] Fixes for various areas under desks
[*] Increased player's overall movespeed: I was initially concerned about the adjustment but I do think it's for the better and the game seems to play the same in all the areas I was concerned about.
[/list]

Thanks again for your patience while I try to discover what to prioritize for the final game

notes.title: Off Shore Demo Available
notes.notes:
[h1]It's Here![/h1]
It's been a bit of a slow road to get here. I started working on various prototypes for new game ideas a year or two ago and I knew I wanted to make a horror game. I want to continue to make games on the side as I work on games professionally during the day but finding the time and energy can be difficult. So back in late June I put together a schedule to create this demo and here we are! This demo represents the last few months of forming loose ideas into more coherent ones and testing what I could do on my own. This demo also serves as a vertical slice to what I'd like for the game to be. I hope people enjoy it and can look past some of the issues to what the game could end up being upon completion.
